UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a registered user of the BharatDarshan Wiki application, allowing for content contributions, profile management, and personalized settings.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

username.description: A unique username chosen by the user for identification within the platform.

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication and identification. (Note: Authentication handled externally)

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

bio.description: A short biography or description provided by the user about themselves.

profileImageUrl.description: URL to the user's profile picture.

memberSince.description: Timestamp indicating when the user registered on the platform.

lastActive.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the user was active on the platform.

preferredLanguageId.description: Reference to the Language entity representing the user's preferred content language. (Relationship: Language 1:N UserProfile)

themePreference.description: The user's preferred theme for the application (light, dark, or device default).

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Defines broad classifications for articles, such as 'State', 'District', or 'Point of Interest', to structure the geographical content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: The name of the category (e.g., 'State', 'District', 'Point of Interest').

description.description: A brief description of what this category represents.

slug.description: A URL-friendly version of the category name for use in navigation or URLs.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents keywords or labels associated with articles for more granular content discovery and filtering (e.g., 'Historical', 'Adventure', 'Religious').

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tag entity.

name.description: The name of the tag (e.g., 'Historical Site', 'National Park', 'Cuisine').

description.description: A description of the tag's purpose or scope.

slug.description: A URL-friendly version of the tag name for use in navigation or URLs.

Article.title: Article
Article.description: Represents a piece of content on the BharatDarshan Wiki, detailing information about a state, district, or point of interest.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Article entity.

title.description: The primary title of the article.

slug.description: A URL-friendly, unique identifier derived from the title for dynamic routes.

content.description: The main textual content of the article, typically in Markdown or HTML format.

categoryId.description: Reference to the Category entity classifying this article (e.g., 'State', 'District', 'Point of Interest'). (Relationship: Category 1:N Article)

parentArticleId.description: Self-referencing foreign key to link an article to its parent (e.g., a 'District' article links to its 'State' article). (Relationship: Article 1:N Article)

authorId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity of the original author of this article. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Article)

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the article was first created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the article was last updated.

version.description: The current version number of the article, incremented with each major revision.

isPublished.description: Indicates whether the article is publicly visible (true) or still in draft/review (false).

latitude.description: The geographical latitude of the place described in the article, if applicable.

longitude.description: The geographical longitude of the place described in the article, if applicable.

tagIds.description: References to Tag entities associated with this article. (Relationship: Article N:N Tag)

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description: Represents a user comment made on an article, allowing for reader interaction and feedback.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Comment entity.

articleId.description: Reference to the Article entity the comment belongs to. (Relationship: Article 1:N Comment)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity of the user who posted the comment. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Comment)

content.description: The text content of the comment.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the comment was posted.

isApproved.description: Indicates whether the comment has been approved for public display (true) or is pending moderation (false).

parentId.description: Self-referencing foreign key to link a comment to its parent comment, enabling threaded discussions. (Relationship: Comment 1:N Comment)

Revision.title: Revision
Revision.description: Tracks historical versions and changes made to an Article, supporting a Wikipedia-like editing history and content recovery.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Revision entity.

articleId.description: Reference to the Article entity this revision belongs to. (Relationship: Article 1:N Revision)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity of the user who made this revision. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Revision)

revisionNumber.description: A sequential number identifying this revision within the article's history, starting from 1.

contentSnapshot.description: A snapshot of the article's full content at the time of this revision.

changesSummary.description: A brief summary provided by the user describing the changes made in this revision.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this revision was created.

MediaAsset.title: MediaAsset
MediaAsset.description: Manages image, video, or other media files uploaded and used within the application's articles.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MediaAsset entity.

filename.description: The original filename of the uploaded media asset.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the media file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'video/mp4').

url.description: The public URL where the media asset is stored and can be accessed.

altText.description: Alternative text for the media asset, crucial for accessibility and SEO.

description.description: A longer description of the media asset, providing context or details.

uploadedByUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity of the user who uploaded this media asset. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N MediaAsset)

uploadedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the media asset was uploaded.

articleIds.description: References to Article entities where this media asset is used. (Relationship: Article N:N MediaAsset)

Language.title: Language
Language.description: Defines the supported languages for content translation within the application, enabling multilingual access.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Language entity.

name.description: The full name of the language (e.g., 'Hindi', 'English', 'Marathi').

code.description: The ISO 639-1 standard language code (e.g., 'hi' for Hindi, 'en' for English).

isRTL.description: Indicates if the language is written Right-To-Left (true) or Left-To-Right (false).

TranslatedArticleContent.title: TranslatedArticleContent
TranslatedArticleContent.description: Stores translated versions of an article's content for multilingual support, generated by AI or human contributors.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TranslatedArticleContent entity.

articleId.description: Reference to the original Article entity this translation belongs to. (Relationship: Article 1:N TranslatedArticleContent)

languageId.description: Reference to the Language entity for which this content is translated. (Relationship: Language 1:N TranslatedArticleContent)

translatedTitle.description: The title of the article translated into the specified language.

translatedContent.description: The main content of the article translated into the specified language.

translatedSlug.description: A URL-friendly, unique identifier for the translated article, if localized URLs are needed.

translatedByUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity of the user who performed or initiated this translation, if applicable. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N TranslatedArticleContent)

translatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this translation was created or last updated.

isAIGenerated.description: Indicates whether this translation was primarily generated by an AI tool (true) or human-edited/created (false).

params.name: articleId
params.description: The unique ID of the draft article.

params.name: commentId
params.description: The unique ID of the comment.

params.name: articleId
params.description: The unique ID of the article this revision belongs to.

params.name: revisionId
params.description: The unique ID of the revision.

definition.description: Media assets uploaded by a specific user. Owned by the 'userId' in the path, ensuring private management while public URLs can be shared in articles.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who uploaded the media asset.

params.name: mediaAssetId
params.description: The unique ID of the media asset.

definition.description: Translated content for published articles. Uses 'languageId' as document ID. Includes 'translatedByUserId'. Denormalizes 'parentArticleAuthorId' and 'parentArticleIsPublished' for authorization independence, allowing contributors to manage translations for public articles.

params.description: The unique ID of the original article.

params.name: languageId
params.description: The unique ID of the language for the translation.

params.name: uid
params.description: The unique ID of the user who has administrative privileges.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for the BharatDarshan Wiki application is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Query as a Security Policy (QAP) to ensure scalability, security, and debuggability. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **Path-Based Ownership:** For user-specific, private data like `UserProfile`s, `UserArticlesDrafts`, and `UserMediaAssets`, the `userId` is embedded directly in the path (e.g., `/user_profiles/{userId}`). This makes authorization rules simple and atomic: `request.auth.uid == userId` for ownership checks, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to other documents to determine access.
2.  **Denormalization for Subcollections:** For subcollections like `Revisions` and `TranslatedArticleContent` that logically belong to an `Article`, critical authorization attributes from the parent `Article` are denormalized into the subcollection documents. Specifically, `Revision` documents will include the `articleAuthorId` and `articleIsPublished` status from their parent article, and `TranslatedArticleContent` documents will include `parentArticleAuthorId` and `parentArticleIsPublished`. This allows security rules to evaluate access based solely on the data within the document and the request context, without requiring a `get()` operation on the parent article. This is crucial for maintaining atomic operations and simplifying rule logic.
3.  **Direct Reference for Comments:** `Comment` documents store their `userId` and `articleId` directly, allowing `request.auth.uid == comment.userId` for personal comment management, and public read access if the parent article is published and the comment is approved.
4.  **Global Roles (DBAC):** Administrative roles are managed via a dedicated top-level collection (`/roles_admin/{uid}`). Authorization rules check for the *existence* of a document at `/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)`, which is an independent and efficient check, adhering to the DBAC principle.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **Structural Segregation for Articles:** The core strategy for QAPs is the segregation of articles into two distinct top-level collections based on their publication status: `/articles_published` and `/user_articles_drafts/{userId}`. 
    *   Documents in `/articles_published` are explicitly published (meaning `isPublished: true` is an invariant for this collection) and are intended to be publicly readable by all. This allows `list` queries on this collection to efficiently retrieve all public articles without security rules needing to filter results, thereby enforcing the QAP principle. 
    *   Documents in `/user_articles_drafts/{userId}` are drafts (`isPublished: false`) and are strictly private to the `userId` in the path. `list` queries on this collection will only return drafts belonging to the authenticated user, again without the rules acting as filters.
2.  **Homogeneous Security Posture:** All documents within a given collection or subcollection (`/categories`, `/tags`, `/languages`, `/articles_published/{articleId}/comments`, etc.) share a uniform security posture. For instance, all `Category` documents are publicly readable, and all `Comment` documents under a published article are publicly readable (subject to `isApproved`). This structural consistency simplifies security rules, making them clear statements of intent rather than complex filtering logic.

By adhering to these principles, the Firestore structure provides a robust foundation for secure, scalable, and easily auditable access control, while efficiently supporting complex queries and multi-language content contribution.
